page: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v7 is an arm64 virtual machine instance within the Dpldsv7 series, provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile provides 48 dedicated 64-bit ARM vCPUs paired with 96.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 2.0 GB per core. The instance does not include discrete GPU hardware accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Integrated local storage is a primary hardware feature of the D48plds_v7, supplying 2,835 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD capacity alongside support for Premium Storage. This expansive local solid-state footprint offers high-throughput, low-latency disk access for temporary data, local caching, and scratch file handling without incurring remote network storage latencies.

The 2.0 GB per core density represents a compute-oriented balance within the general-purpose classification, maximizing CPU core availability for workloads with moderate RAM requirements. This architecture offers cost efficiency for compute-dense scenarios that benefit from ARM efficiency and fast local IOPS, making it suitable for CI/CD compilation, multi-threaded batch jobs, web tier serving, and intermediate data processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v7 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with 48 dedicated arm64 vCPUs, 96.0 GB of memory, and 2,835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core, positioning it as a low-memory, compute-dense option within the Dpldsv7 family. It features zero discrete graphics accelerators. The integrated local NVMe solid-state storage provides low-latency, high-capacity scratch space directly attached to the virtual host. With its balance of high ARM core count, reduced memory footprint, and large local NVMe storage volume, the D48plds_v7 is suited for compute-intensive workloads that require fast local disk throughput, including distributed software compilation, continuous integration runners, high-throughput web serving, and parallel batch data processing.
